title: Keeping the guides current: part of every task
summary: Drake's rule: whoever changes the system updates the guide that describes it, in the same piece of work. A map ties each kind of change to the skill that must absorb it. Replace the untrue rule, cite the new commit, rerun changed examples, open the guide PR (draft if the change is pending), or open an issue if you cannot. I can run a checker that flags a compiler change whose guide was left alone.
goal: Make every change carry its guide update so agents never learn from a stale skill.
key_steps: Check which guide describes what you changed
Edit that guide in the same piece of work, with the new commit and date
Delete the rule the change made untrue
Rerun any changed example against the new pin
Open the guide PR, or an issue if you cannot
Say in the report which guides changed, or why none did

example.code:
note guides: a change that touches what a guide describes must update that guide in the same change
note exit 0 guides current or none affected, 1 a guide is stale, 2 read error
const NR ulong 3
text KW "compiler/\nskills/omega-encoding/\ngates/\nskills/omega-harness/\nwire/\nskills/omega-communication/\n changed; its guide \n was updated in the same change\n was NOT updated: STALE\nGUIDES: no guide affected (say why in the report)\nGUIDES CURRENT\nGUIDES STALE: update the guide before calling this done\n"
note helpers: read all of stdin into inb, walk lines, compare a line prefix with the n-th
note entry of the newline separated table KW, and write table entries, input bytes and numbers
global inb uchar 65536
global num uchar 24
fn rdall to long
t = ulong 0
while lt t len inb bound 65536
k = read 0 inb t sub len inb t
if lt k 0
ret k
end
if eq k 0
ret long t
end
t = add t ulong k
end
ret neg long 27
end
fn eol s ulong n ulong to ulong
i = s
while lt i n bound 65536
if eq get inb i 10
ret i
end
i = add i 1
end
ret n
end
fn kstart k ulong to ulong
p = ulong 0
c = ulong 0
while lt c k bound 4096
if eq get KW p 10
c = add c 1
end
p = add p 1
end
ret p
end
fn klen k ulong to ulong
s = kstart k
i = s
while ne get KW i 10 bound 4096
i = add i 1
end
ret sub i s
end
fn pmat at ulong e ulong k ulong to bool
o = kstart k
m = klen k
if gt m sub e at
ret false
end
for j ulong m
if ne get inb add at j get KW add o j
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn emitk o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 4096
w = write 1 KW add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emiti o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 65536
w = write 1 inb add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emitn o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 24
w = write 1 num add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn say k ulong to void
emitk kstart k add klen k 1
end
fn word k ulong to void
emitk kstart k klen k
end
fn emitu v ulong to void
p = ulong 24
x = v
while true bound 21
p = sub p 1
put num p uchar add rem x 10 48
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
emitn p sub 24 p
end
note each input line is one changed path (git diff --name-only)
note rule r: a path under KW entry 2r changed, so a path under KW entry 2r+1 must change too
fn any k ulong n ulong to bool
s = ulong 0
while lt s n bound 65536
e = eol s n
if pmat s e k
ret true
end
s = add e 1
end
ret false
end
fn rule r ulong n ulong to ulong
t = mul r 2
if not any t n
ret 0
end
word t
word 6
word add t 1
if any add t 1 n
say 7
ret 1
end
say 8
ret 2
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 2
end
n = ulong r
hit = ulong 0
bad = ulong 0
for i ulong NR
v = rule i n
if ne v 0
hit = add hit 1
end
if eq v 2
bad = add bad 1
end
end
if eq hit 0
say 9
ret 0
end
if eq bad 0
say 10
ret 0
end
say 11
ret 1
end

common_mistake: Leaving the guide for later or for a docs owner, or appending a contradicting note under the old rule. Fix: replace the untrue rule in the same change, cite the commit, rerun the example.
evidence_note: The example ran on a Linux AArch64 host (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte with a negative control. Rests on the recorded run of guides.om on three commits in a throwaway repository: stale (exit 1), current (exit 0), no guide affected (exit 0). NOT done: the rule table is a three-rule teaching subset of the real change-to-guide map.
